one_liner: Customizable Rust EVM from alloy-rs with a tail-call, static-table interpreter; claims up to 2x over revm, unpublished numbers.
what_it_does: A Rust library for executing Ethereum transactions, built so that chains can add their own specs, opcodes (via an #[instruction] attribute macro), gas schedules, transaction types, precompiles, environment fields and inspectors through a typed EvmTypes configuration. The API is its own, not revm's: Evm::<T>::new(spec, block, tx_registry, db, precompiles), then evm.transact(&tx)?.commit(). The workspace also ships an EEST state/blockchain test runner, inspectors (including a JS tracer), a CLI that captures and replays mainnet fixtures, and an experimental LLVM JIT/AOT crate.
how_it_is_fast: Opcode handlers are monomorphized into a 256-entry dispatch table per EvmConfig and inspect mode at compile time, so inspector hooks and disabled opcodes cost nothing on the plain path. On nightly rustc, build.rs selects a tail-call threaded interpreter (explicit_tail_calls plus the preserve_none calling convention): each handler takes pc, stack pointer and remaining gas as arguments and jumps straight to the next handler; stable 64-bit builds get a 'packed' table loop instead. Static gas is charged in a pre-step with an unchecked pc advance, and jump-destination analysis is SIMD and lazy (PRs #498 and #492; the SIMD analysis was later ported to revm). Precompiles default to native backends (asm Keccak, libsecp256k1, GMP modexp, blst, MCL BN254, AWS-LC P256).
when_to_use: Building a custom EVM chain or L2 in Rust that needs extra opcodes, precompiles, tx types or gas rules without forking an interpreter.

Throughput-bound single-threaded execution (simulation, replay, block building) where you can run the repo's own revm comparison (EVM2_BENCH_REVM=1 cargo bench -p evm2-cli --bench evm) on your hardware first.
Projects already on a nightly toolchain, which unlocks the tail-call interpreter backend.
Experiments with EVM JIT/AOT compilation via the bundled evm2-jit crate (LLVM 22, Linux or macOS).
when_not_to_use: Consensus-critical production nodes: consensus-rule fixes are still landing weekly (Oct 2026 PRs on EIP-4844 and EIP-7702 validation order, upfront gas saturation, invalid-opcode halts in issue #386).
Code that needs a crates.io release or semver stability: the crate is version 0.1.0, not published on crates.io, and the MSRV (1.96) follows the latest stable Rust.
Many EVM instances in parallel threads: issue #542 (open) shows a process-wide shared Arc for empty Bytecode causing atomic contention, with 30-CPU scaling of only 2.1x (BLAKE2F) to 6.5x (KECCAK256).
Stacks built on revm types and tooling (Foundry, Reth inspectors, revm-based L2 handlers): evm2 is not API-compatible.
Windows users of the JIT, which the LLVM backend does not support.

integration.form: crate (git dependency; not on crates.io as of 2026-10-06)
integration.dependencies: alloy-primitives, alloy-consensus, alloy-eips and related alloy crates; default features also pull C/asm backends: libsecp256k1, GMP (gmp-mpfr-sys), blst, MCL, AWS-LC (aws-lc-rs), asm Keccak. JIT needs LLVM 22.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.96 (edition 2024); nightly rustc enables the tail-call backend automatically
integration.platforms: Any Rust target; no_std with default-features = false; tail-call backend not used on wasm or with the Cranelift codegen backend; JIT Linux and macOS only
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; issue #542 reports cross-thread atomic contention on a shared empty-bytecode Arc when EVMs run in parallel.

gotchas: Interpreter backend depends on the compiler: build.rs picks the tail-call backend only on nightly rustc (overridable with EVM2_DISPATCH_BACKEND), and the CI CodSpeed job builds with stable, so tracked numbers use the packed table loop. The README does not say which backend, toolchain or revm version produced 'up to 2x'.

Harness flaw in crates/cli/benches/evm: the transaction cases are not symmetric. evm2 deep-clones its fully populated InMemoryDB in untimed setup and times transact plus commit, while revm runs on a fresh CacheDB over Arc<InMemoryDB>, so each first-touch account and storage slot is a cache miss plus HashMap insert inside the timed region (and tx.clone() is timed); revm does not commit. This inflates revm's time most on short transactions such as erc20_transfer.

The 21 transaction fixtures have no cross-engine parity check: sanity_check only asserts the call returned Ok, and revm returns Ok for reverted or halted transactions. Only the 10-block mainnet replay diffs gas, success, logs and receipt roots between evm2 and revm (PR #527), and that case times evm2 through the EEST executor but revm through a separate hand-written replay loop.
Heavy unsafe in the hot path (lifetime-erasing raw pointers in the trustme module, unchecked pc advance), which relies on bytecode padding and analysis invariants.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick evm2 over revm (catalogued) for a new Rust EVM variant where interpreter speed matters and you can validate correctness and speed yourself; stay on revm for production maturity and ecosystem compatibility. evmone (C++) is the measured leader on evm-bench and remains the choice for C/C++ hosts via EVMC; no independent run places evm2 against evmone or Guillotine.
verified_claims_summary: The only claim is a first-party README line, 'up to 2x faster than revm', with no table, workloads, hardware, toolchain, backend or revm version. The repo carries a Criterion harness that runs revm 43 next to evm2 on 21 transaction fixtures and a 10-block mainnet replay when EVM2_BENCH_REVM=1 is set, but CI does not set it and no output is published.
status_note: Very active under alloy-rs (last commit 2026-10-05, 619 commits, 72 stars, MIT OR Apache-2.0), but pre-release (0.1.0, not on crates.io) with consensus fixes still landing; treat as experimental.
